items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Roscoe, who was a hustler, a young, handsome hustler, he owned this joint. That was the first time I saw Billie Holiday. We went in there, me and Smitty, and we sat down.

ctx.x: That's where it was, Squares, down on 63rd Street.

Yes. It was the type of bar where the barmaid made a whole lot of tips, just being there. The people would go there to see her, to talk to her. Because that's the way they idolized her. Chicago was a town where you still could live on your reputation. People still accepted... It's a notoriety town, word-of-mouth. "So-and-so is at such-and-such a place," and you went there, and you paid homage to whoever it was.

Well, I was out at the Nest Club. And upstairs over the Nest Club was the Mad House. And Roscoe, who was a hustler, a young, handsome hustler, he owned this joint. That was the first time I saw Billie Holiday. We went in there, me and Smitty, and we sat down. A girl come out the back, this fine-looking, brownskin girl, very defiant, and she starts bitchin' with some guys to give her some money.
